title: Valid Parentheses
keyIdea: A closing bracket must match the most recently opened one that's still open. That's last in, first out, so a stack. Push openers; on a closer, the top must be its partner (pop it). Fail on a mismatch, on a closer with an empty stack, or on openers left at the end.

approaches.name: Keep deleting matched pairs
approaches.idea: Repeatedly remove any adjacent "()", "[]" or "{}". A valid string shrinks to nothing.
approaches.why: Each pass scans and erases in O(n), and up to n/2 passes are needed (e.g. "((((...))))").

approaches.name: Stack
approaches.idea: Push every opener. For a closer: empty stack → false; top isn't its partner → false; otherwise pop. At the end the stack must be empty.
approaches.why: One pass; each character is pushed or popped at most once. The stack can hold up to n openers.

quiz.q: Why does a stack fit this problem?
options: The last bracket opened must be the first one closed (last in, first out)

quiz.q: Why isn't counting each bracket type enough?
options: "([)]" has equal counts but closes in the wrong order
At the end: the stack still holds two openers
At index 0: a closer arrives while the stack is empty

steps: Which characters can appear? Is an empty string valid? What exactly makes a string invalid?
Trace "{[()]}" and "([)]" by hand. Where does the second one go wrong?
Deleting matched pairs until nothing changes: why is it O(n²)?
Closers match the most recent open bracket: which data structure is last in, first out?
What do you push? What do you check on a closer? What's left to check after the loop?
Code it, naming the three ways to return false as you write them.
Dry-run "(()" and ")(": which of the three failures does each hit?
Time and space? How would you return the length of the longest valid substring (LC 32)?
